definitions.explanation: A single written or spoken sentence. Used when referring to the structure or content of written text.

examples.japanese: {一文|いちぶん}が{長|なが}すぎる。
{一文|いちぶん}を{短|みじか}くすると{読|よ}みやすくなる。
examples.english: Making each sentence shorter makes it easier to read.

examples.japanese: この{手紙|てがみ}の{最後|さいご}の{一文|いちぶん}に、{彼|かれ}の{気持|きも}ちがこめられている。
examples.english: His feelings are packed into the last sentence of this letter.

notes:
USAGE:
{一文|いちぶん} refers to a single sentence in writing. It is commonly used when discussing writing style, editing, or text structure.
Do not confuse with {一文|いちもん} (one mon — a tiny amount of money), which has a different reading and meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一文|いちぶん}が{長|なが}い (a sentence is long)
- {一文|いちぶん}を{短|みじか}くする (to shorten a sentence)
- {最後|さいご}の{一文|いちぶん} (the last sentence)
- {一文|いちぶん}で{言|い}い{表|あらわ}す (to express in a single sentence)
